judge.reason: It asserts an explicit formula for every set \(\mathcal S_r\), which a team could try to prove. This differs from e1, which asserts that all these sets are empty.
judge.gate: It explicitly specifies the entire set for every integer r≥2 and includes its finite boundary point 1/r.

options.counterfactual: For every fixed graph H with chromatic number r+1 and ex(n,H)=t_r(n)+O(n), a simultaneous edge-and-cycle maximizer exists for every sufficiently large n. Consequently, every set S_r is empty.
options.approach: Try to prove the simultaneous-maximizer statement using extremal stability and a comparison of cycle counts in graphs close to the balanced complete r-partite graph. Identify the precise structural assertion needed rather than invoking an unverified theorem.

options.counterfactual: For every fixed graph H with chromatic number r+1 and ex(n,H)=t_r(n)+O(n), a simultaneous edge-and-cycle maximizer exists for every sufficiently large n. Consequently, every set S_r is empty.
options.approach: Recheck odd-wheel candidate constructions, including their forbidden-subgraph status and cycle-count asymptotics. Locate any error that makes an apparent conflict with the universal statement disappear.

options.counterfactual: For every fixed graph H with chromatic number r+1 and ex(n,H)=t_r(n)+O(n), a simultaneous edge-and-cycle maximizer exists for every sufficiently large n. Consequently, every set S_r is empty.
options.approach: Separate the deduction that S_r is empty from the theorem it requires. Formulate that theorem precisely and assess whether it can be established from available extremal-graph results.

options.counterfactual: There is a fixed graph H with ex(n,H)=t_r(n)+O(1) for which infinitely many orders have no simultaneous edge-and-cycle maximizer. Thus 0 belongs to S_r for at least one r.
options.approach: Search for forbidden graphs whose edge-extremal constructions have a bounded exceptional configuration containing both added within-part edges and deleted between-part edges. Compare whether cycles assign different marginal values to those two kinds of edges.

options.counterfactual: There is a fixed graph H with ex(n,H)=t_r(n)+O(1) for which infinitely many orders have no simultaneous edge-and-cycle maximizer. Thus 0 belongs to S_r for at least one r.
options.approach: Focus on r=2 and odd orders, where adding an edge to the larger bipartition class can affect cycles differently from adding one to the smaller class. Seek a fixed forbidden graph that forces edge maximization to choose the less cycle-efficient configuration.

options.counterfactual: There is a fixed graph H with ex(n,H)=t_r(n)+O(1) for which infinitely many orders have no simultaneous edge-and-cycle maximizer. Thus 0 belongs to S_r for at least one r.
options.approach: Attempt to prove that a bounded additive extremal correction guarantees a simultaneous maximizer. Under this counterfactual, the first failed step should expose the exceptional structure needed for a counterexample.

options.counterfactual: The first obstruction to simultaneous maximization comes from competing bounded-size tree components inside a single part, rather than from odd wheels or other standard forbidden graphs. The boundary of S_r is controlled by the shapes of those trees as well as their edge density.
options.approach: Derive a cycle-count expansion for complete r-partite graphs with bounded-degree graphs added inside one part. Determine how the edge count and the number of adjacent edge pairs contribute to the first terms that can distinguish competing tree components.

options.counterfactual: The first obstruction to simultaneous maximization comes from competing bounded-size tree components inside a single part, rather than from odd wheels or other standard forbidden graphs. The boundary of S_r is controlled by the shapes of those trees as well as their edge density.
options.approach: Compare repeated stars and repeated paths of the same order, allowing a bounded exceptional component to give one construction an extra edge. Determine whether the other construction can compensate through a larger cycle count.

options.counterfactual: The first obstruction to simultaneous maximization comes from competing bounded-size tree components inside a single part, rather than from odd wheels or other standard forbidden graphs. The boundary of S_r is controlled by the shapes of those trees as well as their edge density.
options.approach: Investigate whether a single forbidden graph H can enforce the proposed competition between tree-component types. Establish that realizability before treating examples for a forbidden family as examples for this problem.

options.counterfactual: The proposed eight-vertex graph does not establish that 1/3 belongs to S_2: its structural argument or cycle comparison contains a substantive error.
options.approach: Audit the structural lemma in the supplied workspace, checking each passage from stability to uniform cross-density and each extension of a local configuration to H. This would distinguish a repairable omission from a failure of the claimed extremal characterization.

options.counterfactual: The proposed eight-vertex graph does not establish that 1/3 belongs to S_2: its structural argument or cycle comparison contains a substantive error.
options.approach: Independently derive the exact cycle counts for the two proposed constructions by contracting their internal paths. Compare the resulting generating functions and limiting constants without relying on the supplied derivation.

options.counterfactual: The proposed eight-vertex graph does not establish that 1/3 belongs to S_2: its structural argument or cycle comparison contains a substantive error.
options.approach: Search for an H-free construction that exceeds the claimed extremal function or an additional edge-extremizer not covered by the characterization. Either would identify why the proposed edge–cycle separation does not follow.

options.counterfactual: The coefficient 1/3 is not the lower boundary of S_2; some fixed three-chromatic forbidden graph witnesses membership at a smaller coefficient.
options.approach: Investigate forbidden graphs whose extremal constructions add matchings rather than disjoint three-vertex paths to a complete bipartite graph. Such constructions have linear correction approximately n/4 and are the natural first candidates below n/3.

options.counterfactual: The coefficient 1/3 is not the lower boundary of S_2; some fixed three-chromatic forbidden graph witnesses membership at a smaller coefficient.
options.approach: Examine whether finitely many exceptional vertices or missing cross-edges can separate edge and cycle maximizers when the main internal graph is a matching. A constant edge advantage could compete with the first lower-order term in the cycle count.

options.counterfactual: The coefficient 1/3 is not the lower boundary of S_2; some fixed three-chromatic forbidden graph witnesses membership at a smaller coefficient.
options.approach: Study the structural alternatives forced by an extremal bound strictly below t_2(n)+n/3. Identifying all possible internal components could either produce a smaller counterexample or narrow the search to a finite collection of structural types.

options.counterfactual: For some r at least three, S_r contains 0: bounded additive excess over the Turán number can already permit infinitely many orders with no simultaneous edge-and-cycle maximizer.
options.approach: Analyze complete r-partite graphs modified on a fixed number of vertices, allowing both internal edges and missing cross-edges. Compute their first nonvanishing cycle-count differences to determine whether fewer edges can be offset by a more favorable placement of the modifications.

options.counterfactual: For some r at least three, S_r contains 0: bounded additive excess over the Turán number can already permit infinitely many orders with no simultaneous edge-and-cycle maximizer.
options.approach: Look for a structural gap in the heuristic that bounded additive excess forces interchangeable finite modifications of balanced Turán graphs. In particular, examine whether exceptional vertices impose part-size constraints that prevent an edge-extremizer from attaining the cycle-optimal balance.

options.counterfactual: For some r at least three, S_r contains 0: bounded additive excess over the Turán number can already permit infinitely many orders with no simultaneous edge-and-cycle maximizer.
options.approach: Test whether adjoining complete multipartite components to a three-chromatic construction can yield an example with bounded additive excess at higher chromatic number. Track both the extremal correction and the cycle comparison, since increasing the chromatic number can change their relationship.
